minutes.headline: Committee voted to recommend raising the capital project threshold, and to back the deferred FY21 capital articles at Special Town Meeting.
minutes.summary: The Capital Planning Committee approved prior minutes, then agreed to recommend to the select board a higher minimum for capital projects, with a useful-life test as an alternative. It reviewed the deferred FY21 capital projects for the special town meeting and voted to recommend them. It then set out the schedule of department presentations and how the threshold change will reach the select board.

Recommend to the board of selectmen that the minimum dollar amount for a capital project be set at thirty thousand dollars or an estimated life extension of five or more years
Recommend approval of the deferred articles at the special town meeting, including the unexpended article funding

what_happened.line: The committee voted to recommend a higher minimum for what counts as a capital project, or else a project that extends an asset's life by five or more years.
The committee voted to recommend the deferred FY21 capital articles at the special town meeting, including the article using unexpended capital funds.
Members described the current threshold as too low and discussed several higher figures before the motion was made.
Police and fire presentations were tentatively set for November 3, then weekly Tuesdays starting the 10th; the schedule is to be firmed up and sent.
The threshold recommendation will go to the finance committee for review before it reaches the select board; the chair will put it together.

why_it_matters: A higher threshold means fewer items are planned and funded through the capital process, and more are handled in the regular operating budget.
The deferred FY21 capital articles are on the special town meeting warrant, so residents there will be asked to vote on them and on a deposit to the capital reserve fund.
